Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, west Triangle, Quezon City http: Ilwww. dilg.gov.ph s. 20.11 MR. SAUL A. ESTABLECIDA Sangguniang Bayan (SB) Secretary Municipality of Burdeos, Quezon Dear SB Secretary Establecida: OPINION NO. 23 JAN 201b This has reference to your letter dated 24 April 2017, requesting this level's opinion and/or clarification on DILG-LegaI Opinion No. 15, S.2014 quoting your following concerns: 1. Since the performance standards of Sangguniang Bayan (SB) members is not measured on their attendance, does it construed that their Record of Attendance should not be the baseline for the computation of their Terminal Leave Benefits (TLB)? 2. If it happened that the aforesaid benefits is granted based on their attendance during Sessions, does it entitle them to claim for the deficiency of payment on their services; and 3. Will it be binding if the inclusion of a standard measure in the Internal Rules of Procedure (IRP) which provides for the Record of Attendance as basis in computing the TLB of SB members. Hence, the instant request. At the outset, please be informed that neither the Local Government Code (LGC) of 1991 nor any regulation has fixed the office hours of elective officials. The rationale for this is understandable for it violates the very nature of the work of elective officials who are considered on call anytime of the day. Fixing their working hours unnecessarily delimit their services to the prejudice of their constituents and ultimately the public service (DILG Opinion No. 24, S.201()). In other words, the nature of work of elective officials should not be confined and limited to attending sessions. Be that as it may, local elective officials are also entitled to leave credits as provided in Section 5 of Civil Service Commission (CSC) Memorandum Circular (MC) No. 14, S. 1999, entitled "ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS AND AMENDMENTS TO CSC MC NO. 41, S. 1998': to wit:

"Sec. 5 — Leave credits of local elective officials — Local elective officials ARE entitled to leave privileges effective May 12, 1983 pursuant to Batas Pambansa 337 and Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 7160). SAID LEAVE CREDITS SHALL BE COMMUTATIVE AND CUMULA TIVE't However, if they will be absent during their session for personal reasons, they have to file their respective leaves of absence, following the procedures/guidelines laid down in Section 47(a)(2) of the LGC, viz: "(2) Leaves of absence of vice-governor or a city or munici vice-mayor shall be approved by the local chief executive concerned: Provided, That the leaves of absence of the members Of the sanggunian and its employees shall be approved by the vice-governor or city or municipal vice- mayor concerned". Further, Section 77(b)(I) of Rule XIV of the Implementing Rules and Regulations of the LGC states that Elective local officials shall be entitled to the same leave privileges those enjoyed by appointive local officials, including the cumulation and commutation thereof. Nevertheless, pursuant to CSC-Memorandum Circular (MC) No. 2, S.2016, the Commission, in view of the enactment of R.A. No. 9849, entitled "ANA C/' DECLARING THE TENTH DAY OF ZHUL HIJJA, THE TWELFTH MONTH OF THE ISLAMIC CALENDAR, A NATIONAL HOLIDAY FOR THE OBSERVANCE OF EIDULADHA, FURTHER AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 26, CHAPTER 7, BOOK T OF EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 292, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE ADMINISTRATIVE CODE OF 1987, AS AMENDED', includes Eidul Adha and Eidul Fitr among the regular holidays now being observed in the Philippines, to change the constant factor used in computing the TLB, increasing the number of legal holidays from IO to 12. The formula for the computation of TLB is provided under the DBM Budget Circular (BC) No. 2002-1, S.2002, and CSC-MC No. 14, S. 1999 to wit: Where: TLB = Terminal Leave Benefits s = Highest monthly salary received D = Number of accumulated vacation and sick leave credit CF = ConstantFactorwhichis .0481927 (CSCMC. No. 2, S.2016)

Payment of terminal leave as provided in Section 37 of CSC-MC No. 14, S. 1999 is given to any official/employee of the government who retires, voluntary resigns, or is separated from the service and who is not otherwise covered by special law, such official/employee is entitled to the commutation of his/her leave credits exclusive of Saturdays, Sundays and Holidays without limitation and regardless of the periods when the credits were earned. It is understood from the stated provision that the leave credits mentioned refers to vacation and sick leave credits, consistent with the above given formula. In view of the foregoing, TLB should not be computed based on the record of attendance during Sessions as the substance and computation thereof is already provided for by the abovementioned Circulars. Thus, the second query negates claim for the deficiency of payment on their services as TLB is not granted based on their attendance during the Sessions. Third, the inclusion of attendance in the IRP as basis in computing the TLB is not binding for the same reason, DILG Legal Opinion No. 15, S.2014 is not applicable in T LB, further, the computation and funding of TLB is governed by DBM Budget Circular No. 2002-1, S.2002 (with amendment as to Constant Factor provided by CSC-MC No. 2, s.2016). Please be apprised that what has been clarified in DILG Legal Opinion NO. 15, S.2014 is the grant of Representation and Transportation Allowance (RATA) as provided in Local Budget Circular No. 103, S.2013. Finally, the said opinion is not applicable to TLB as the same is governed by DBM- BC No. 2002-1, S.2002. Further, this Department already addressed a similar concern as stated in DILG-Legal Opinion No. 12, S.2016, pertinent portion of which reads: "Local Budget Circular No. 103, S.2013, as discussed in DILG Opinion No. 15, S.2014, is inapplicable to claims for refund on deductions of terminal leave credits. Note that the computation and funding Of terminal leave benefits is governed by DBM Budget Circular No. 2002-1, s.2002. Clearly, DILG Opinion No. 15, S.2014 is inapplicable to terminal lea ve benefits. " We hope to have guided you accordingly. Very truly yours, By autho of the Secretary: AUS ERE A. PANADERO Undersecretary CC: DIR. MANUEL Q. GOTIS Regional Director DILG-Region IV-A (CALABARZON)
